{{Quote|Fast now! I want a clean sweep... no survivors!|Beilert Valance|<ref name="marvel16" />}}
In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], the notorious [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Beilert Valance/Legends|Beilert Valance]] led his crew in a '''wholesale slaughter''' of the neutral and unarmed medical center [[Anglebay Station]] on [[Telos IV]]. Formerly a promising [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] [[Stormtrooper Commander/Legends|commander]], Valance had suffered grievous wounds in [[Assault on Doniphon|battle]] and taken to Anglebay Station, where he was rebuilt with [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] parts. Unable to continue his [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] service, Valance entered into a life as a bounty hunter, but despised his [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] parts and kept his true form a secret even from his own crew. Wanting to destroy the past and eliminate any record of his treatment, Valance ordered his crew to join him in attacking and completely annihilating the station. Valance's crew stormed the hospital and immediately began murdering patients and staff, with particular malice being shown to the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] that Valance so despised. After Valance personally obliterated Anglebay Station's computer records, he and his crew took off, triggering explosions that completely destroyed the hospital.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|MY FACE! WHAT HAVE YOU DONE TO MY FACE?|Beilert Valance reacts to his new cybernetic parts on Anglebay Station|<ref name="Serving the empire">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-11-serving-the-empire|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 11: Serving the Empire}}</ref>}}
[[File:Termivalance.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Beilert Valance was rebuilt with cybernetic parts at Anglebay Station.]]
A cunning and brilliantly talented young [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] [[Stormtrooper Commander/Legends|commander]], [[Beilert Valance/Legends|Beilert Valance]] was expected to achieve great things in the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]. Instead, that chapter of his life ended, quite suddenly,<ref name="tnms">{{SW|url=news/the-not-so-magnificent-seven|text=The Not-So Magnificent Seven|int=The Not-So Magnificent Seven|nolive=1}}</ref> on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]]<ref name="teaoc">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> of [[Doniphon]]. During the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] campaign known as the [[Kwymar Suppressions]], Valance led Imperial ground forces that were strafed from above by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], suffering grievous wounds. Near-[[Death/Legends|death]], Valance was taken to [[Anglebay Station]], an unaligned medical station on [[Telos IV]], and left to suffer his fate. But rather than perish, Valance was rebuilt with [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] parts, ending his career in the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] but giving him a new life as a [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]].<ref name="wizards2">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=swminis/article/huntwithin2|text=The Hunt Within: Valance's Tale: Part 2|int=The Hunt Within: Valance's Tale: Part 2}}</ref>

His life forever changed, Valance decided to contribute to Imperial justice in a different way: as a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]]. After his ordeal, Valance became dangerously unhinged: his loathing of his half-mechanical state and the end of his military career manifested itself in a violent hatred of all [[Droid/Legends|droids]], and an increased disposition towards brutal violence. Meanwhile, he had become single-mindedly obsessed with an unnamed "[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|farmboy]]" who had been involved in the Rebel [[Rescue of Princess Leia/Legends|rescue]] of [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] from the Imperial [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]], wishing to punish the fugitive for his apparent friendship with [[C-3PO/Legends|two]] [[R2-D2/Legends|droids]]. Assembling a crew on the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] known as the ''[[Kill Switch]]'', Valance led his men on hunts and raids across the Outer Rim,<ref name="tnms" /> all the while going to great lengths to hide his cyborg state. Eventually, feeling the need to destroy all evidence of his past, Valance ordered his men to attack and completely destroy Anglebay Station, including all the sick and wounded patients staying there. Although the planned massacre did not sit easy with Valance's veteran crew, he offered enough [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|money]] that the plan went ahead with no defections.<ref name="tnms" />

==The battle==
{{Quote|Good grief! There must be some error. This facility is neutral. Even the Empire, Re-"<br />"Shut up... junk!|A droid orderly and Beilert Valance during the raid|<ref name="marvel16" />}}
[[File:TheVteam-MSW16.png|thumb|right|250px|Beilert Valance leads his raid on Anglebay Station.]]
Valance's attack on Anglebay Station was carried out with maximum speed, efficiency, and brutality. Without warning, Valance's crew blasted a hole in the side of the hospital and stormed the facility, executing medical staff as they went. Valance gave the honor of rounding up and destroying Anglebay Station's [[Unidentified robot orderly|robot orderlies]], to whom particular malice was reserved, to his second-in-command, [[Slssk]]. Meanwhile, Valance proceeded to his main objective: the station's computer records, which contained information on his treatment and his cyborg body. Valance laid waste to the record room, killing several [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] in the process, ensuring that any data on his treatment was wiped.<ref name="marvel16" />

Meanwhile, Slssk, [[Remel Fud]] and several other of Valance's crewmen invaded the in-patient bays, moving from room to room and executing whoever they found. In one of those bays, they encountered a [[Don-Wan Kihotay|dying, delirious man]] babbling in his sick bed. However, before they could kill the man, his ravings took an interesting turn: he started to speak of wanted Imperial fugitive [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], a [[Lepi/Legends|Lepi]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] named [[Jaxxon/Legends|Jaxxon]] and an unnamed, mysterious "boy" with a [[FE-9Q|droid]]. Slssk and Fud immediately rushed to Valance with the information, which piqued his interest, as Solo was a known associate of Valance's farmboy, and had a large [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on his head besides. His next objective in mind, Valance boarded the ''Kill Switch'' and set off, triggering a series of explosions in his wake that completely annihilated Anglebay Station and left no survivors.<ref name="marvel16" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|But that's the past... I've destroyed that! Now there's the boy. The boy and his droids...|Beilert Valance, after the raid on Anglebay Station|<ref name="marvel16" />}}
The babblings of the dying old man on Anglebay Station led Valance to believe that his path to Solo, and therefore his elusive "farmboy," led through Jaxxon. As such, Valance sent Fud to track him down on the Lepi's base on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]].<ref name="tnms" /> Although Jaxxon managed to evade capture, the ''Kill Switch'' followed him and his partner [[Amaiza Foxtrain/Legends|Amaiza Foxtrain]] to the Outer Rim [[Farm/Legends|farmworld]] of [[Aduba-3/Legends|Aduba-3]], where they had gone to warn the "boy" of Valance's hunt. Valance and his crew got to Aduba-3 not long after, but almost immediately blundered into a trap set by Jaxxon, Foxtrain and a group of local [[Onacra|villagers]], leading to the death of many of Valance's men in a [[Bantha/Legends|bantha]] stampede. Valance himself survived the attack only to realize that Jaxxon's "boy" wasn't the Rebel he was searching for: rather, he was a local farmer named [[Jimm Doshun]], who some months before had helped Jaxxon and Solo [[Battle of Aduba-3|defend]] his village from a [[Cloud-Riders/Legends|swoop gang]]. Realizing his mistake, Valance broke into a fit of hysterical laughter, before blasting back off into the stars to continue his hunt alone.<ref name="marvel16" />

==Behind the scenes==
Beilert Valance's attack on Anglebay Station appeared in [[Star Wars (1977) 16|''Star Wars'' (1977) 16]], written by [[Archie Goodwin]] and released in [[1978]]. In its appearance, the battle was illustrated by [[Walter Simonson|Walt Simonson]].<ref name="marvel16" />
